feature: Arrow and measurement Appearance: Arrow, Chip, Color, Marker, Size, and the rest under Advanced
summary: A picked arrow now shows just its Arrow style, Chip style, one Color, Marker and an S M L Size, with every part folded under a closed Advanced that says where each colour comes from. A measurement gets the same rows without the Arrow row.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: arrow-appearance-simple-walk and measure-appearance-simple-walk.

try.do: Press A, drag an arrow on a screenshot, type a label and press Command-Return.
try.shotNote: Left: the prototype. Middle and right: the app. Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click L on the Size row (or right-click the arrow, Chip Size, Large): the label's words and padding grow and the line thickens.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click S: the label and line shrink.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click Show beside Advanced: Line and Head say from Color, Chip Fill and Chip Text say from style.
Drag the Line swatch onto Chip Text: Chip Text now shows Reset, the others still say where they come from, and the warning under Color offers Reset Colors.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick Blue in Color: the line, head and chip turn blue but Chip Text keeps the colour you gave it. Click its Reset to hand it back.
Measure a gap (I), pick it, open Advanced: Caliper from Color, Chip Fill, Edge and Text from style, and Size beside Marker.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: With Advanced closed, is anything you reach for every day now hidden?
Is the step from M to L big enough to be worth a control (it follows the design system's 12 to 14 points)?
Does from Color / from style / Reset tell you at a glance which parts you have changed?
Should Advanced stay open once you have opened it (it does now, across arrows and launches)?
rough: The walks' pointer clicks on panel controls do nothing on this Mac since about 21:50 on 2026-10-31, on the committed code too, so both new walks fail at their first pointer press after passing everything before it (layout, right-click sizes, from-labels, painting by hand). Logged with a reproduction on walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26; the pictures of the open fold were taken with the fold's saved setting turned on instead of a click.

Color is a label over its swatches with a ninth Custom well, where the prototype puts eight dots on the label's line; the Custom well and the row came from any-colour-you-pick-for-an-arrow-or-measurement.
Opacity, Blending and Masked by sit above the Arrow row as on every layer, which the prototype leaves out. Placement by UX-PATTERNS placement contract: Appearance leads with what every layer has.

Advanced goes further than the prototype: Ends (the tail's cap), Label size and corners, and for a measurement Chip size, Unit and Role live there too. A typed Label or Chip size overrides Size and lights none of S, M and L.
Chip Edge on a Solid pill is switched off, so its row shows its switch and no from-label until it is switched on.
Size changes an arrow's line to 3, 4 or 5 px with S, M and L; a measurement's caliper keeps its 1 to 3 px hairline. Head Size is a multiple of the line, so it follows.
A fresh arrow is still drawn in #FF3B30, which is not one of the eight swatches, so the Custom well is lit on a new arrow. Left as it is.
